key_insight: Instead of enumerating which subsets of temporal properties are realizable, the authors compute in a single fixed-point pass a state-to-goal-set relation and synthesize strategies that maximize the set of satisfied properties, using a fully symbolic encoding to handle exponentially many combinations.
problem_solved: LTLf synthesis when multiple (possibly conflicting) properties are specified and satisfying them all may be impossible; avoids combinatorial explosion from enumerating property subsets while producing optimal (maximal) realizable guarantees.
method: Construct a product game and compute a single fixed-point relation mapping game states to the sets of goals realizable from them.
Synthesize strategies that achieve maximal realizable goal sets rather than checking each subset separately.
Use a fully symbolic encoding: introduce Boolean goal variables and exploit monotonicity to compactly represent exponentially many goal combinations.
impact: Enables scalable synthesis of controllers/planners that optimally trade off multiple temporal requirements; useful for verification, planning, robotics and other systems where not all specifications can be satisfied simultaneously.
visual_elements: Diagram of a product game with arrows to a matrix/list of realizable goal-sets (state → achievable-goals relation).
Flowchart of the single fixed-point computation and strategy extraction pipeline.
Iconic depiction of Boolean goal variables compressing 2^n goal combinations (e.g., many circles collapsing into a compact symbolic block).
Comparison chart showing exhaustive subset enumeration vs. the symbolic fixed-point approach (time/space or scalability).
paper_authors: Christoph Weinhuber, Yannik Schnitzer, Alessandro Abate, David Parker, Giuseppe De Giacomo
